When belling repeated attempts at a blocked formalisation, do NOT set a
hard stop at N attempts. Joe, 2026-08-19: *"I'm happy to continue exploring, and
you're the one that came up with the hard-stop criteria, not me. If Codex is
making progress, usually that converges in my experience."*

**Why:** attempt-count is not the informative variable; whether the OBSTRUCTION
CHANGES is. On the t02A06 bridge-3 work, two stops on chart-label dependence were
the same wall and stopping was correct; the third stop solved that and hit a
distinct `Fin` castSucc/succ transport problem — convergence, not repetition, and
my attempt-counting rule would have parked live progress.

enough to compare with the previous one — that comparison IS the stopping
criterion. Same wall twice → stop and escalate. Wall moved → continue. Watch for
the inverse failure in yourself: if you keep recommending "one more bounded
attempt", you are the one ratcheting, and the fix is to say so out loud rather
than to quietly grant it. Related: [[topology-build-pm-seat]].
